page: Vultr vx1-m-2c-16g-120s is a memory-optimized virtual server belonging to the VX1 Cloud Compute family. It features an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor running at 2.0 GHz, configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs derived from 1 physical core with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is provided via a bundled 120 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. No GPU hardware is present.

Performance benchmarks indicate a strong single-core profile but limited multi-core scaling due to the dual-vCPU configuration. Single-core stress-ng tests, single-threaded gzip compression, and single-threaded bzip3 decompression all rank in the top 25 percent tier. Conversely, multi-core benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core and Geekbench multi-core, fall into the bottom 25 percent category. Memory bandwidth is also relatively low, with uncached read and write speeds of 26.94 GB/sec and 24.91 GB/sec respectively. Database operations and medium-model LLM text generation show poor performance, placing in the bottom 10 percent.

This server offers a qualitative cost-efficiency advantage for workloads requiring a larger memory footprint without demanding high parallel processing power. The dedicated AMD EPYC vCPUs ensure consistent single-threaded execution, but the low physical core count limits its suitability for heavy multi-threaded tasks, software compilation, or complex database operations. It is best suited for lightweight memory-bound applications, single-threaded processing pipelines, basic text processing, and small-scale web serving where 16 GB of RAM is necessary but high CPU concurrency is not required.
